A newer shared worker question is hidden and cannot be cleared from a machine with an older question

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Functional. Needs you can keep asking for a review-loop choice after another machine records and publishes it. `needs_you` passes the `best` state to `person_waits`; a local worktree wins a tie against the fetched branch when their step counts match. `--resolve` saves the choice without adding a step, so the stale local `stop` remains unchosen. `person_waits` then reports it even though the pull-request record contains the wait's end.
findings.title: Disputed keep 6: a choice made on another machine remains in Needs you

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Functional. After machine B answers question Q1 and its worker asks Q2, machine A can still hold Q1's `question_id`. The filter here excludes the open Q2 from A's Needs you, despite Q2 being in the pull-request record. On A, `forge work --note` also prefers that stale local ID in `worker.py:145`, ending Q1 again and leaving Q2 open. This breaks the promised same-machine view and answer flow during a normal handoff.
findings.title: A newer shared worker question is hidden and cannot be cleared from a machine with an older question

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. The new guide promises that stuck-worker choices appear on every machine through the pull-request record, but the refresh here runs only after a worker round. `worker.py:210` can call `close.stuck_round`, whose `stuck_stop` records an owner wait and refuses before this refresh. The size-limit path in `close.py:193` likewise refuses before its publish. A teammate therefore cannot see either open choice wait or how long it has waited.
findings.title: Not done: publish stuck-worker choice waits
